A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MiraGe research. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results on Kodak and DIV2K, camera and Gaussian-count ablations, and manual editing and physics-simulation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds editing and physics comparisons, DIV2K ablations, inpainting examples, and rendering-speed and storage measurements.

M1.justification: v2 adds optional inpainting after image manipulation to fill exposed gaps, with outputs illustrated in Figure 11. This extends the editing workflow; the Gaussian parametrization, Amorphous/2D/Graphite variants, mirror-camera training and reconstruction loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds explicit block-wall collision and domino-contact test scenarios in Figure 12, extending the physical interaction conditions demonstrated. Kodak, DIV2K, Animals and generated-image coverage remain. Extending appendix ablations to DIV2K does not introduce a new dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the reconstruction comparator set. v2 adds actual qualitative comparisons against DragGAN for editing locality and pose manipulation (Figures 8 and 10), and PhysGen for physical interactions (Figure 12), substantially expanding comparison of the central editing capabilities. DragDiffusion is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The retained reconstruction experiments keep their stated splits, resolutions and metrics. New Table 4 introduces a Kodak camera-setting evaluation using FPS, uncompressed storage and storage after .spz compression. These are additional evaluation procedures, without evidence that the original reconstruction protocol changed.

E4.justification: v2 extends the camera and initialization-count ablations from Kodak to DIV2K (Tables 2–3), adds camera effects on rendering speed and storage (Table 4), and examines inpainting as mitigation for editing gaps. New DragGAN and PhysGen cases also investigate preservation of unrelated features and collision behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All Table 1 values and retained Kodak entries in Tables 2–3 are identical. v2 adds DIV2K ablation results, Kodak FPS/storage measurements and qualitative editing, inpainting and physics findings. For example, new Table 2 entries report DIV2K Amorphous PSNR of 46.00 with one camera and 54.54 with mirror cameras; these are newly reported conditions, not gains over v1.

T1.justification: The covariance construction, Gaussian-to-triangle mapping and inverse, spatial constraints, quaternion construction and mirror-training objective are retained. Equations are abbreviated and renumbered, without substantive new mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of state-of-the-art reconstruction, manipulation of 2D images with apparent 3D effects, and integration with physics engines. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations about preserving unrelated features compared with generative edits and describes the mirror camera as confining Gaussians between the cameras. It qualifies the exposed-background limitation with inpainting mitigation. Limitations concerning non-generativity, large edits and parameter cost remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies Blender 3.6 and the Lattice modifier, explicitly states reuse of 3DGS pruning/densification, documents .spz compression, and adds project-page and tool pointers. The listed GPUs, license, quaternion implementation and future-tense code-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens the existing INR/Gaussian positioning with interactive 2D editing: DragGAN, DragDiffusion, bounded biharmonic weights and linear-subspace deformation. PhysGen and inpainting also enter the comparison and discussion, establishing relationships to methods directly relevant to the editing contribution. Several application-oriented citations disappear with the social-impact rewrite.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted language revisions, condenses parts of related work, separates the mirror-camera explanation, rewrites social impact and expands appendix explanations. Social impact and the FPS discussion move into the appendix. The main section sequence and much of the abstract, method and conclusion prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and extensively resizes and relocates figures and tables. Several original editing illustrations and the FPS plot move to the appendix. New comparison figures are added, the gap illustration gains inpainting outputs, Tables 2–3 gain DIV2K blocks, and Table 4 is introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 provides better evidence for practical editing through direct DragGAN/PhysGen comparisons, broader ablations and explicit rendering/storage costs (Tables 2–4). Inpainting examples and expanded related work also improve context. The gain is incremental: reconstruction scores and the core method remain unchanged, while the new editing comparisons are qualitative and provide limited protocol detail.
